To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
68Ga-ssA PET parameters correlated with a circulating neuroendocrine tumor transcript signature and disease status could be predicted from a quotient of gene expression and 68Ga- ssA PET parameters.

68Ga-somalostatin analog positron emission tomographic imaging parameters correlated with circulating NET transcript signatures and that disease status could be predicted from an elevated quotient of MORF-4-L2 gene expression and imaging parameters.

the maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax values) measured in two centers are comparable, the circulating gene transcript signature correlates well with SUVmax values and the gene expression quotient (MORF42L2) and the SUVmax value can predict disease status.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that can be utilized for disease monitoring and to predict disease status.
the development and application of novel molecular biomarkers for NET diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis.
the identification and validation of a novel biomarker panel for NETs.

the NETest can be considered as a surrogate for the 68Ga-ssat PET/CT.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
68Ga-ssat is a very good imaging agent to assess the presence of NETs, however it is unable to determine whether the disease is stable, progressive, or regressive.
a blood test can define disease status in NETs and can be used in conjunction with imaging.
68Ga-ssA PET imaging and circulating NET gene transcripts can be combined to improve the management of patients with NETs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
circulating gene transcripts are a reliable and robust biomarker that can be used for the diagnosis of NETs and for the evaluation of treatment response in NETs.

the circulating gene expression signature is a strong biomarker for NET disease status and can predict the response to therapy, and the imaging parameters are a strong biomarker of NET disease status.
circulating NET gene transcript levels correlate with 68 Ga-SSA PET/CT imaging and can define disease progression.
